newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's Inapa to boost exports in 96.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Inapa to boost exports in 96.

text.p: Portuguese paper firm Inapa-Investimento, Participacoes e Gestao expects to raise exports to 70 percent of its total production by the end of 1996 from 60 percent at the end of 1995, its president said.
"There is a strong appetite abroad for the high quality paper produced by Inapa in Portugal," Vasco Pessanha told Reuters in an interview.
The main foreign markets for Inapa's paper are Spain and Britain.

Pessanha said Inapa would invest 4.5 billion escudos this year to upgrade its factory in Setubal, 30 km (20 miles) south of Lisbon, which should raise production by 40 percent to 280,000 tonnes per year.

"Our aim is to produce 350,000 tonnes per year at the end of the decade by upgrading our machinery, a process which will begin at the end of this year and will allow us to produce 280,000 tonnes of paper in 1997," he said.
Pessanha said Inapa expected to raise sales in 1996 to 50 billion escudos from 49.5 billion in 1995 and profits to between 0.8 and 1.0 billion escudos from 0.351 billion in 1995.
Inapa posted a consolidated net profit of 0.4 billion escudos in the first half, a 33 percent increase from the same period a year ago.
